title: Arithmetic and Geometric Sequences
standard_text: Recognise and use sequences of triangular, square and cube numbers, simple arithmetic progressions, Fibonacci-type sequences and simple geometric progressions; deduce expressions for the nth term.
meta_desc: Free Year 11 GCSE maths worksheets on arithmetic and geometric sequences, the nth term and term-to-term rules. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Arithmetic: add the same number. Geometric: multiply by the same number.
key_sub: Quadratic sequences have a constant second difference.
body_html:
How it works

An arithmetic sequence adds the same number each time (the common difference). Its nth term is dn + c.

A geometric sequence multiplies by the same number each time (the common ratio).

A quadratic sequence has a constant second difference. The n² coefficient is half the second difference.

Example

Find the nth term of 5, 8, 11, 14, …

Common difference 3

3n gives 3, 6, 9, …; add 2

Answer: 3n + 2

Example

Find the nth term of 2, 7, 14, 23, …

First differences 5, 7, 9; second difference 2

n² gives 1, 4, 9, 16; subtract: 1, 3, 5, 7 = 2n − 1

Answer: n² + 2n − 1

Common mistakes

  • Writing n + 3 for 5, 8, 11, … (the difference 3 goes in front of n).
  • Using the whole second difference as the n² coefficient instead of half of it.
  • Adding instead of multiplying for a geometric sequence.

faq.q: How do you find the nth term of an arithmetic sequence?
faq.a: Find the common difference d. The nth term is dn + c, where c makes the first term correct.

faq.q: How do you find the nth term of a quadratic sequence?
faq.a: Find the second difference and halve it to get the coefficient of n². Subtract that n² part from each term, then find the nth term of what is left.
A sequence where each term is the one before multiplied by the same number, the common ratio, such as 3, 6, 12, 24.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 3, 6, 12, 24, 48, …
items.e: Each term is the one before × 2, so it is geometric.

items.q: What is the next term? 5, 25, 125, 625, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by 5 each time. 625 × 5 = 3,125.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 18, 22, 26, 30, 34, …
items.e: The difference is always 4, so it is arithmetic.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 7, 21, 63, 189, 567, …

items.q: What is the next term? 1, 4, 16, 64, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by 4 each time. 64 × 4 = 256.

items.q: What is the next term? 10, 6, 2, −2, …
items.e: This is arithmetic: subtract 4 each time. −2 − 4 = −6.

items.q: What is the next term? 19, 22, 25, 28, …
items.e: This is arithmetic: add 3 each time. 28 + 3 = 31.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, …
items.e: The differences change (2, 3, 4, 5) and there is no common ratio, so it is neither.

items.q: What is the next term? 4, −2, −8, −14, …
items.e: This is arithmetic: subtract 6 each time. −14 − 6 = −20.

items.e: This is arithmetic: add 8 each time. 23 + 8 = 31.

items.q: What is the next term? 13, 22, 31, 40, …
items.e: This is arithmetic: add 9 each time. 40 + 9 = 49.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 6, 10, 15, 21, 28, …
items.e: The differences change (4, 5, 6, 7) and there is no common ratio, so it is neither.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, …
items.e: The differences change (5, 7, 9, 11) and there is no common ratio, so it is neither.

items.q: What is the next term? 5, −15, 45, −135, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by −3 each time. −135 × (−3) = 405.

items.q: What is the next term? 3, 12, 48, 192, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by 4 each time. 192 × 4 = 768.

items.q: What is the next term? 2, −4, −10, −16, …
items.e: This is arithmetic: subtract 6 each time. −16 − 6 = −22.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, …
items.e: The differences change (9, 11, 13, 15) and there is no common ratio, so it is neither.

sets.title: The nth term of arithmetic sequences

items.q: What is the nth term of −9, −15, −21, −27, …?
items.e: The difference is −6, so start with −6n. The 1st term of −6n is −6; to get −9, subtract 3. −6n − 3.

items.q: What is the nth term of 7, 6, 5, 4, …?
items.e: The difference is −1, so start with −n. The 1st term of −n is −1; to get 7, add 8. −n + 8.

items.q: What is the nth term of −14, −16, −18, −20, …?
items.e: The difference is −2, so start with −2n. The 1st term of −2n is −2; to get −14, subtract 12. −2n − 12.

items.q: What is the nth term of 11, 17, 23, 29, …?
items.e: The difference is 6, so start with 6n. The 1st term of 6n is 6; to get 11, add 5. 6n + 5.

items.q: What is the nth term of 11, 13, 15, 17, …?

items.e: The difference is 2, so start with 2n. The 1st term of 2n is 2; to get −6, subtract 8. 2n − 8.

items.q: Each term is the term before divided by 2. What is the next term? 400, 200, 100, 50, …
items.e: 50 ÷ 2 = 25. The common ratio is ½.

items.q: Each term is the term before divided by 2. What is the next term? 64, 32, 16, 8, …
items.e: 8 ÷ 2 = 4. The common ratio is ½.

items.q: What is the common ratio of 6, 24, 96, 384, …?
items.e: Divide a term by the one before: 24 ÷ 6 = 4.

items.q: A geometric sequence has common ratio 2. Its 4th term is 16. What is its 1st term?
items.e: Divide by 2 3 times: 16 ÷ 8 = 2.

items.q: The sequence 3, 9, 27, … is geometric. What is the 5th term?
items.e: Keep multiplying by 3: 3, 9, 27, 81, 243. The 5th term is 243.

items.q: The sequence 5, 15, 45, … is geometric. What is the 5th term?
items.e: Keep multiplying by 3: 5, 15, 45, 135, 405. The 5th term is 405.

items.q: What is the nth term of the quadratic sequence −9, −10, −9, −6, −1, …?
items.e: Second difference 2, so the n² coefficient is 2 ÷ 2 = 1. Subtract n² from each term and find the linear part: n² − 4n − 6.

items.q: What is the second difference of the sequence 1, 5, 13, 25, 41, …?
items.e: Find the first differences, then the differences between them: 4.

items.q: What is the next term of the Fibonacci sequence 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, …?

items.q: A geometric sequence has a1 = 5 and r = 2. Which is a8?
What is the next triangular number? 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, …
items.e: The differences go up by 1: +2, +3, +4, +5, so add 6: 21.

items.q: A theater has 20 seats in row 1, 23 in row 2, 26 in row 3, and so on. How many seats are in row 15?
A bacteria population doubles every hour. It starts at 50. How many are there after 5 hours?
items.e: 50 → 100 → 200 → 400 → 800 → 1,600. This is a geometric sequence with ratio 2.

items.q: Grace saves £5 in week 1, £8 in week 2, £11 in week 3, and so on. How much does she save in week 10?
items.e: The nth term is 3n + 2. Week 10: 3 × 10 + 2 = £32.

items.q: A ball is dropped from 200 cm. Each bounce reaches half the height of the one before. How high is the 3rd bounce?
Patterns are made from sticks: 4, 7, 10, 13, … sticks. How many sticks are in pattern 20?
items.e: The nth term is 3n + 1. Pattern 20: 3 × 20 + 1 = 61.

items.q: Patterns are made from sticks: 4, 7, 10, 13, … sticks. Which pattern uses 100 sticks?
The nth term of a sequence is 50 − 4n. What is the first negative term?
Which sequence has the nth term 5 − 2n?
A car worth £16,000 loses half its value every 3 years. What is it worth after 9 years?
Find the missing term in the geometric sequence 3, ☐, 75, 375, …
items.e: The ratio is 375 ÷ 75 = 5, so 3 × 5 = 15.

items.q: Find the missing term in the arithmetic sequence 7, ☐, 19, 25, …
items.e: The difference is 6, so 7 + 6 = 13.

items.q: Which is the nth term of 2, 4, 8, 16, …?
items.e: Each term is a power of 2: 21, 22, 23, … so the nth term is 2n.

items.q: Which is the nth term of 1, 4, 9, 16, …?
items.e: These are the square numbers: n2.

items.q: Ethan says 2, 6, 18, 54, … is arithmetic because the numbers go up. Is he right?
c: No, it is geometric with ratio 3
items.e: The differences are 4, 12, 36, which are not equal. Each term is × 3: geometric with ratio 3.

items.q: The 5th term of an arithmetic sequence is 23 and the 6th term is 27. What is the 1st term?
items.e: The difference is 4. Go back 4 steps from the 5th term: 23 − 16 = 7.

items.q: A sequence starts 3, 7, and each term is twice the term before minus 1. What is the 4th term?
How many terms of 7, 11, 15, 19, … are less than 100?
items.e: The nth term is 4n + 3. 4n + 3 < 100 when n < 24.25, so 24 terms.
